title: The world tables record the revision they came from, and a game server started against another revision's tables extracts them again
notes: 3.23: the game server extracts the character name and level tables into an empty world database and records the install's revision with each set in client_extraction.

The run then marks the level tables as an older revision's and starts the game server again, which extracts them again and records the install's revision; the name tables, still current, are left as they are.
No wizard enters the world: the client stays at its login screen.
server_log_allowed: character_create_school holds no school, so no wizard can be created until it does
realmlist holds no realm, so no player can be sent to a gameserver until one is added

steps.name: the name tables record the install's revision
steps.query: SELECT revision FROM client_extraction WHERE kind = 'names'

steps.name: the level tables record the install's revision
steps.query: SELECT revision FROM client_extraction WHERE kind = 'levels'

steps.name: mark the level tables as an older revision's
steps.statement: UPDATE client_extraction SET revision = 'r1.Older', extracted_at = 1 WHERE kind = 'levels'

steps.name: the game server sees the level tables came from another revision
steps.pattern: The world database's levels came from r1\.Older, and the install is now .*, so they are extracted again

steps.name: the game server extracts the level tables again
the level tables record the install's revision again
steps.query: SELECT revision FROM client_extraction WHERE kind = 'levels' AND extracted_at > 1

steps.name: the client at its login screen throughout
